Apple today accused a new UK proposal targeting App Store fees as tantamount to price regulation, warning that the move could harm innovation and investment. Details below.

Apple fights back against App Store regulation in the UK

According to a Reuters report, Apple today submitted a formal response to the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) consultation, opposing a proposed rule that would allow app developers to link to alternative payment options.

The CMA can impose such requirements after designating Apple and Google as having 'strategic market status' in their respective mobile platform markets. Under the UK's new digital markets regime, this designation allows the regulator to introduce company-specific rules to promote competition and give consumers more choice.

Under the proposal, Apple and Google could still charge commissions to developers who complete transactions via alternative payment methods, but any such fees would have to be deemed 'fair and reasonable'.

Reuters noted that the CMA 'expects the guiding fees to be lower than current App Store charges, with the savings passed on to UK consumers or reinvested in developers' businesses to support innovation'.

However, Apple disagrees and has pushed back against the proposal. Here's the Reuters report:

The CMA has rejected Apple's characterisation of the proposal as price regulation, saying its aim is to set out principles for determining whether guiding fees are fair and reasonable, rather than directly setting the level of those fees.
